transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-03
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martin (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sam Rivera (NovaHealth CTO), Maya Chen (Lead ML Eng), Jordan Lee (Platform PM), Tara Singh (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
- Demo of Redwood model catalog, selecting open models, benchmarks and compatibility matrix.
- Discussion of hosted vs dedicated/private (VPC) options, SOC2/KMS, quantization trade-offs.
- Agreed next steps: share compatibility matrix, supply prompts/logs, schedule perf run.

Topics: model catalog walkthrough, benchmark metrics (latency/cost/throughput), compatibility matrix (quantization/hardware), VPC/KMS/SOC2 concerns, pilot/perf run scope.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we good to start?
[00:06] Sam: Yeah, this is Sam, thanks. I think we have about 40 minutes, excited to see the catalog and how it maps to our latency needs.
[00:12] Maya: Hi, Maya here. Our main ask is low-latency clinical summarization, plus cost guidance.
[00:18] Jordan: Jordan - I'll watch from an infra perspective, mostly interested in compatibility and private options.
[00:25] Priya: Great. Alex will run the high level and I'll jump into the console and the compatibility matrix.
[00:32] Alex: Cool. Quick context: Redwood's model catalog has curated open models plus performance profiles — we show latency p50/p95, throughput, token cost estimates and recommended quantization profiles per hardware. Today we'll demo selecting an open model and running the benchmark profiles, then Priya will show the compatibility matrix.
[00:50] Sam: When you say "recommended quantization" is that pre-validated? We have concerns about hallucination regressions when using int8-ish quantization.
[01:00] Priya: Good question. We annotate models with recommended quant levels and we run model-quality regression tests on our eval suite. It's not perfect, we recommend running your prompt set as well. We can flag models that have known degradation for summarization tasks.
[01:15] Maya: Okay — we will definitely want to run our prompts. We'll also want to check tokenization differences — our clinical text has weird tokens.
[01:23] Alex: Absolutely. We'll share a prompt set upload link. For the demo, I'll open the console.
[01:32] [01:32] Alex: (screen) Here's the catalog. You can filter by task — summarization, chat, embeddings — or by model family: Llama-3 variants, RW-Open, Mistral, etc.
[01:46] Alex: You can see a card for each model with p50/p95 latency on our standard 8k context, cost per 1k tokens and compatibility tags for hardware and quantization.
[01:56] Maya: Are these numbers for hosted API or dedicated?
[02:01] Alex: These are our standard hosted benchmarks on our production fleet — we also surface dedicated and private-profile numbers separately; the console toggles between hosted/dedicated/private views so you can compare.
[02:12] [02:12] Priya: I'll jump into the compatibility matrix tab. This is a matrix we maintain showing which models are validated on which accelerators (A100, H100, T4, Neuron, etc), supported quant levels, and any known caveats (KV cache size differences, memory blowups).
[02:28] Priya: For example, Llama-3-13B-Open shows support across A100/H100 with int8/int4 recommended profiles; there's a note about sequence-length scaling on T4 that can bump latency.
[02:40] Jordan: Cool, can we export that matrix? We need to feed to our procurement and infra people.
[02:45] Priya: Yes, there's an export CSV/PDF button. We'll send the official PDF as well.
[02:50] Sam: On benchmarks — what's your p95 numbers for the Llama-3-13B on H100 for a 2k prompt?
[02:58] Alex: Our console shows roughly 190–230ms p50 and 420–480ms p95 for 2k context on H100 with int8-ish profile on hosted. That's on our standard load; dedicated/private could be tighter depending on provisioning.
[03:14] Maya: That's promising. Our SLO is 500ms p95 for critical endpoints, so that could work. What's the cost per 1k?
[03:22] Alex: The card estimates about $0.12 per 1k tokens for that model on hosted with the int8 profile; again dedicated pricing differs.
[03:30] Jordan: Do you support model fallbacks? We want automatic degrade to a cheaper model during burst to avoid errors.
[03:37] Priya: Yes, routing policies support fallbacks — you can define a primary model and fallback to a quantized variant or a cheaper family. The console lets you create those policies.
[03:46] [03:46] Alex: Let me show the benchmark details — clicking into the model we have graphs: latency distribution, throughput across concurrencies, and a small table of benchmark inputs used. The UI links to raw artifacts and our benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:58] Sam: Are those spreadsheets editable or just read-only? We might want to run our own runs and compare.
[04:04] Priya: The shared sheet is copyable. We'll share the raw artifacts and the run scripts — the same harness we use internally so you can reproduce locally or on a private cluster.
[04:14] Maya: About private clusters — we have strict PHI rules. Is Redwood Private viable for air-gapped or VPC-only network?
[04:24] Alex: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and an on-prem package; we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management and produce audit logs for every request.
[04:34] Tara: On audit logs — do you keep token-level logs or only metadata? We cannot store patient data in cleartext.
[04:40] Priya: By default we capture request metadata and hashes for content; for PHI workloads customers can opt for no-capture mode where the payload never leaves customer's environment in private deployments. We'll share the SOC2 + architecture docs.
[04:52] Sam: Good. Can you run a sample perf test against a private cluster if we give you a short-term access? We want to see end-to-end latency including network on our VPC.
[05:02] Alex: Yes, we support scheduled perf runs and can coordinate a slot. For that we'd need a contact in your infra and an agreed test plan.
[05:12] Jordan: We have a cloud infra team, will share an infra contact in the next steps.
[05:17] [05:17] Alex: Back to the model: I'll show the eval metrics. For each model, we show quality regressions over time using our eval harness; you can upload reference prompts and we'll run model-vs-model comparisons.
[05:30] Maya: Does the eval harness surface hallucination metrics or factuality scores?
[05:35] Priya: We have a suite that includes entailment-style checks, and we run Rouge/BLEU-style metrics as appropriate; for hallucination we use a mixture of model-based detectors and human-labeled gold sets. We can add your clinical metrics if you provide them.
[05:50] Sam: How does the console present tokenization differences? We saw earlier tokenization variations can change cost significantly.
[05:57] Alex: There's a tokenization preview tool — paste sample text, pick a model, and it shows token counts and tokenized sequence. That helps you tune prompts and estimate cost.
[06:07] Maya: Nice. Can we set alerts if token counts spike unexpectedly?
[06:12] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route alerting for token usage, latency, and error rates. Alerts can trigger email, webhook, or PagerDuty.
[06:20] [06:20] Sam: About compatibility matrix — does it list supported CUDA/cuDNN versions and driver caveats?
[06:26] Priya: We include hardware + driver matrix in the doc. For private/on-prem we list recommended drivers and any known kernel-level caveats. We also note if a model requires a new runtime build for optimized kernels.
[06:38] Jordan: We use mixed GPU fleet (A100 + older T4). Can you do automatic routing so that large models go to high-memory nodes and smaller loads to cheaper GPUs?
[06:47] Alex: Absolutely — the smart routing policies allow you to route by model size, latency SLO, and cost. You can tier by region and GPU class; policies are first-class objects in the console.
[06:57] Maya: Can we do traffic-splitting between quantized and float variants for A/B?
[07:03] Priya: Yes, rollouts allow canary and A/B testing across model variants; we record quality and cost metrics for each variant so you can compare.
[07:11] [07:11] Alex: I'll open an example rollout we use internally: 10% traffic to a quantized variant, 90% to baseline; after a 24-hour window the console aggregates eval metrics and can auto-rollback on regressions.
[07:23] Sam: That auto-rollback is useful. Do you have SLA commitments for Dedicated?
[07:28] Alex: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers in contract. We'll share the SLA doc.
[07:33] Tara: For compliance, do you support SAML SSO and RBAC integration with our IdP?
[07:38] Priya: Yes, SAML/SSO, SCIM, and fine-grained RBAC are supported in Private and Dedicated. Hosted customers get SSO via IdP integrations as well.
[07:48] Jordan: Let's talk about bench repeatability — can you show a benchmark run?
[07:53] Alex: Sure, I'll initiate a quick run for Llama-3-13B on a hosted H100 node with our standard 2k prompt set. It should take ~3–5 minutes to populate the console with results.
[08:03] [08:03] Alex: (starts run) Running... while that goes, any questions?
[08:09] Maya: If you're running hosted benchmarks, how do you prevent noisy neighbors from skewing numbers?
[08:14] Priya: We run on isolated test pools for benchmark runs with controlled concurrency and run multiple trials to get stable stats; we also surface the confidence interval and raw traces so you can inspect fluctuations.
[08:27] Alex: The run completed, pulling up charts — you can see throughput vs concurrency and latency percentiles. p95 is roughly in the numbers I mentioned earlier.
[08:38] Sam: Do you expose KV cache hit rates? For summarization we expect repeated patient context to hit the cache.
[08:45] Priya: Yes, cache metrics are exposed. You can enable prefix caching and we track hit/miss ratios per key. That can bring down tok/sec and cost significantly for repeated contexts.
[08:56] Jordan: About model variants — do you host customer-built fine-tuned models in the same runtime?
[09:02] Alex: Yes, customers can upload fine-tuned artifacts or reference a container; we provide versioning, can pin to hardware classes, and handle kernel selection. For private deployments, artifacts can remain in your registry.
[09:14] Maya: For our clinical model we might want to run smaller context windows but heavier reasoning. Can the catalog show tradeoffs for context vs latency?
[09:24] Priya: The model pages include charts for different sequence lengths; we also provide midpoint estimates for token cost. You can run custom benchmarks with your sequence-length distributions.
[09:35] Sam: How do you measure quality across quantized variants?
[09:40] Priya: We run paired evaluations on the same prompt set and compute delta metrics; we also highlight deltas that exceed thresholds for clinical-explainability metrics.
[09:49] [09:49] Alex: I'm going to open the compatibility export now and show the CSV. It lists GPU, quant support, driver reqs, notes about memory and KV.
[09:59] Jordan: Looks good. Can that be versioned per model release? We have to track when a model changed behavior.
[10:05] Priya: Yes, compatibility entries are timestamped and tied to model versions; console shows a history.
[10:12] Maya: Any known issues with tokenizer differences between Llama-3 forks?
[10:17] Alex: There are minor differences; we surface tokenizer snapshots and recommend normalization steps.
[10:23] Sam: Regarding pricing — hosted is straightforward pay-as-you-go, but for Dedicated how do you handle overage or burst?
[10:31] Alex: Dedicated has reserved capacity with optional burst pools; overage is billed per-usage at agreed rates. We can propose a hybrid commit+burst model.
[10:40] Jordan: Does Redwood Optimize offer suggestions on batching/caching to lower cost?
[10:44] Priya: Yes — the Optimize toolkit analyzes request traces and suggests batching windows, cache TTLs, quant profiles and even model family recommendations for given latency/cost targets. It can export a config you can apply.
[10:56] Maya: Can Optimize simulate cost impact before applying changes? We need to show finance the delta.
[11:02] Alex: It produces a projected cost delta based on historical traces; it's an estimate but usually accurate within a margin.
[11:10] [11:10] Sam: Any limitations for PHI-heavy workloads in Optimize?
[11:14] Priya: For PHI you'd run Optimize on traces that remain in your VPC/private deployment. We can also run a sanitized analysis if needed.
[11:23] Jordan: Can Optimize recommend quantization levels per route?
[11:27] Priya: Yes, per-route recommendations with confidence and expected quality impact.
[11:34] Maya: Will you be able to tag models as "not recommended for PHI"?
[11:38] Alex: You can annotate models and create policy guards in the console to prevent certain models from being used by protected routes.
[11:46] Sam: Okay, let's talk timeline — if we wanted to pilot in 3 weeks what would you need?
[11:51] Priya: Ideally sample prompts, a rough traffic profile, infra contact for private perf run, and any compliance constraints. We'll then propose a pilot plan and provide an estimated cost.
[12:02] Jordan: We'll gather that.
[12:07] [12:07] Alex: Quick note — we also have a benchmark workbook that lists our test harness and raw artifacts, link: https://redwood-inference.example.com/benchmarks/novahealth-sample (note: placeholder link). We'll attach the export after the call.
[12:20] Maya: Perfect. Any example of a private perf run SLA?
[12:25] Priya: We generally commit a window and provide a run report: latency histograms, traces, and recommendations. We'll include a run template.
[12:35] Sam: For tokens and storage — does Redwood support encrypted-at-rest only or bring-your-own-key?
[12:41] Priya: Bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM is supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports customer-managed keys for encryption at rest in higher-tier plans.
[12:52] Tara: Will that integrate with our existing AWS KMS?
[12:56] Alex: Yes, we have integrations for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and common HSM providers. We'll provide the integration guide.
[13:06] [13:06] Alex: We're about 30 minutes in; I'll do a quick recap then hand to next steps. Recap: demoed model catalog, compatibility matrix, benchmark run, discussed private/VPC options, KMS/SOC2/compliance, Optimize recommendations, and pilot steps.
[13:23] Jordan: Sounds good. A couple more quick questions: do you provide per-route cost attribution to product teams?
[13:30] Priya: Yes, cost breakdown by token, by route/model, and by user/token-level is available in Console; you can export for chargeback.
[13:40] Maya: Is streaming supported for summarization? We need partial results while rendering UI.
[13:44] Alex: Streaming is supported — partial tokens, delta updates, and we support function calling and structured outputs if you want deterministic JSON responses.
[13:54] Sam: For our acceptance criteria — we want p95 < 500ms on critical routes and <10% quality delta vs baseline fine-tune. Is that a reasonable pilot objective?
[14:03] Priya: Yes that's reasonable to test in pilot. We'll help define the acceptance test.
[14:10] [14:10] Alex: Final logistics: I'll send the compatibility matrix PDF, benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2/KMS docs, and a pilot run template. Priya will follow up on the tech notes. Maya will share prompts/logs. Jordan will send infra contact.
[14:25] Maya: We'll do that. Thanks.
[14:28] Sam: Great, thanks Alex and team.
[14:31] Alex: Thanks everyone — talk soon.

End of transcript. (Some words may be transcribed imperfectly; speaker labels approximate.)
